title: Beef and vegetables (no carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens, potatoes, gravy)

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of lean beef stewed with a mix of vegetables (such as bell pepper, zucchini, tomatoes and onion) without carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens, potatoes or gravy. Beef provides a high‑quality source of protein, while the vegetables add vitamins, minerals and fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is one of the richest sources of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.
Gentle simmering preserves most of the vegetables’ vitamins compared with rapid boiling.
Excluding potatoes lowers the dish’s glycemic index, making it more suitable for blood‑sugar control.
A gravy‑free preparation usually contains less sodium, beneficial for people with high blood pressure.
The combination of beef and vitamin‑C‑rich vegetables enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef supplies all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: High in iron
items.content: The iron in beef supports normal hemoglobin levels and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: Vitamin C from vegetables
items.content: Bell pepper and tomatoes provide vitamin C, which boosts immunity and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Fiber and antioxidants
items.content: Zucchini and onion add dietary fiber and antioxidants that support digestive health.

items.title: Low carbohydrate content
items.content: Without potatoes or gravy, the dish fits well into low‑carb eating plans.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Even lean beef contains saturated fats, which should be limited in heart‑disease diets.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: If heavily salted, the dish can be problematic for those with hypertension.

items.title: Potential pathogens
items.content: Beef must be cooked to a safe internal temperature to avoid salmonella or other bacterial risks.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, optionally with whole‑grain sides such as quinoa or brown rice. Vegetables can be eaten together with the beef or separately. Fresh herbs like parsley or basil add aroma and extra nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the cooked dish to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.
